scope: The Salta Cathedral basilica exterior around the 2008 photograph publication, including the pink and cream main front, twin open bell towers, nave, side aisles, crossing dome and choir. The nearby Archbishop’s Palace, separately identified structures and interiors are outside the model.

originalReview.notes: The oblique plaza view shows the pink wall planes, cream trim and classical columns, three large entry arches, central decorated gable and blue lobed opening, four-sided upper belfry openings, and the small clock on the eastern return.

quallaSearch.notes: Qualla was checked first. The exact published photograph is a Hugopujszo first-party public-domain release. The other local candidate is a laundry storefront. The camera day is unavailable and the native upload date is used as the era anchor. The Argentina national heritage text establishes the crossing dome and Latin-cross plan. No supplemental imagery was used.
